subject: Release notes approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy (sign-off)
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2026 at 5:19 PM PST
Subject: Release notes approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy (sign-off)

Dylan, Elliot —

Can you both sign off on the proposed approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy for the model changelog before we lock the v1 implementation? I’d like to treat this as the “default contract” Product/Eng/Docs will operate under.

TL;DR proposal (v1):

1) Workflow states (for customer-visible notes)
- draft: auto-generated by worker; editable by authorized internal users
- in_review: requires explicit submission; freezes most fields except “reviewer comments”
- published: immutable (corrections are handled via superseding entry; original remains visible in history)

2) Who can do what
- Editors (Product + Release Eng + Support Readiness): can edit drafts, submit for review
- Approvers (Product lead + Docs lead): can approve and publish (either one can block)
- Emergency publish path: Release Eng can publish with retroactive approval required within 1 business day (audit event recorded)

3) Customer-safe wording policy (guardrails)
- Default to plain language; no internal model nicknames, vendor/procurement details, or hardware/region capacity notes
- Always include: Impact (who is affected), Compatibility (API/tooling), and Rollback guidance (if applicable)
- Allowed content includes links to eval dashboards, but no raw internal metrics or “internal-only” runbook links
- Deprecations must include timeline + replacement model/version + what to change

Docs / requirements references:
- PRD requirements: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/customer-visible-model-changelog-requirements
- Style guide draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/DX/model-release-notes-style-guide
- Change management policy: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/POL/model-version-change-management-policy
- Linear: https://linear.redwoodinference.com/issue/PM-803

Two open points I need you to weigh in on:
A) Perf deltas: do we ever include token/s or latency changes as numbers? Current recommendation is “qualitative only” unless we have a customer-facing benchmark page to link.
B) “Known issues” language: Support wants a short “Known issues / mitigations” section. Docs team previously flagged this as risky if it reads like an incident report.

If you’re OK with the above as-is, please reply with “Approved” + any non-blocking edits. If not, please call out blockers.

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2026 at 6:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release notes approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy (sign-off)

Approved, with a couple notes (non-blocking, but I’d like us to capture them explicitly):

- Emergency publish path: +1 for having it, but we should be crisp on when it applies (security/policy, material customer impact, or legal). Otherwise it will become the default bypass.
- Immutability: strong +1 on “supersede only.” Please make sure the publish action always emits an audit event with actor + reason.
- Perf deltas: I agree with qualitative only for v1. If we add numbers later, we should standardize units and the evaluation environment or it’ll become a support nightmare.

Re: “Known issues,” I think it’s fine if:
- it’s constrained to customer-observable behavior + workaround (no internal RCA language)
- it’s optional and only present when we have something actionable

If Elliot is aligned, I’m comfortable treating this as the standard.

Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Sponsor
Redwood Inference


From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2026 at 7:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release notes approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy (sign-off)

Approved from Docs, with language constraints we should bake into the style guide (and ideally lint for):

- Avoid “regression”/“degraded” unless we also provide a customer action. Prefer “We identified an issue affecting…” + mitigation.
- Avoid “we changed kernels / quantization / routing” unless it directly maps to a customer-visible compatibility note (e.g., tool calling supported, context window changed). The how is almost always internal.
- “Known issues” section is OK if framed as “Known limitations” and only includes:
  - Symptom
  - Who is impacted (e.g., function calling on model X)
  - Workaround or “contact support”

On your open points:
A) Perf deltas: agree with no numbers in v1. If we need to say something, say “improved throughput” or “reduced latency” and link to a customer-facing benchmark page once it exists.
B) Known issues: agree with Dylan’s constraints. Also: no dates/times that look like incident comms.

One more suggestion: In the “Impact” section, standardize a single sentence template. Example:
“Impact: No action required for pinned versions. Customers on floating aliases may see behavior changes starting <date>.”

Elliot

—
Elliot Price
Docs Lead, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 29, 2026 at 8:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release notes approval workflow + customer-safe wording policy (sign-off)

Thanks both — I’ll incorporate the notes as “non-negotiables” in the policy doc + style guide.

Decisions captured (v1):
- Perf deltas: qualitative only; no numbers unless we have a customer-facing benchmark page
- Known issues: renamed to “Known limitations,” optional, and must include workaround/action (no RCA/incident tone)
- Emergency publish path: restricted to (a) security/policy, (b) materially customer-impacting accuracy/behavior issues, or (c) legal/compliance. Requires reason string + retroactive approval within 1 business day.
- Publish + supersede must always emit audit event (actor + reason)
- “Impact” section uses a standardized first sentence (Elliot’s template)

I’ll update the Confluence pages today and tag you in comments for final skim. If no objections by EOD, we’ll treat it as locked for ENG implementation.

Marissa
